# Kourovka Problem 9.59 (subformations of the formation generated by a finite group)

The proposition that for every finite group $G$ there are only finitely many formations contained in the formation generated by $G$ (the intersection of all formations containing $G$). Classes of finite groups are predicates on finite groups; a formation is closed under homomorphic images and finite subdirect products ($G/N_1, G/N_2 \in \mathfrak F \Rightarrow G/(N_1 \cap N_2) \in \mathfrak F$), the empty class included.

Source: E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 9.59 (A. N. Skiba and L. A. Shemetkov (after W. Gaschütz)).
